sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC. It extracts every replica `orders` row with `updated_at` later than the high-water mark minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports can make a row visible up to 90 minutes after its `updated_at`. The document does not explain the mechanism beyond that.
sonnet.q3: The edit raises the row's `updated_at`. The next nightly extract pulls it (it is later than mark minus 2h). Merge upserts it into `fact_orders` by `order_id` because the staged `updated_at` is at least the existing one.
sonnet.q4: The app sets `deleted_at`, which also updates `updated_at`. The row is extracted like any change. Merge sets `is_deleted` to true in `fact_orders`, and the row stays (no hard delete).
sonnet.q5: The run is marked `failed` in `etl_runs`. The scheduler reruns the whole nightly from the start, up to 2 more times, 15 minutes apart. After the third failed attempt it pages on-call. The mark has not moved, so the next 02:00 run covers the gap.
sonnet.q6: The document does not say what dashboards show at 06:00 beyond that they see either the whole night or none of it (so the previous state). The check at 06:00 UTC posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts if there is no succeeded nightly row for today's UTC date. A later finish still commits.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares row count and checksum per creation day over the last 30 days, finds the mismatched day, and reloads all of that day's orders from the replica.
sonnet.q8: Staging keeps only the highest-`updated_at` row per `order_id`. Merge upserts into `fact_orders` by `order_id` only where the staged `updated_at` is at least the existing one, so an older copy never overwrites a newer one. Merge is safe to repeat.
sonnet.q9: It is stored in `etl_watermark`, a one-row warehouse table. The value is the highest `updated_at` in staging (unchanged if staging is empty). It is set during merge, in the same transaction as the upsert and the run-succeeded mark.
sonnet.q10: Merge into `fact_orders`, moving the mark and marking the run succeeded all happen in one warehouse transaction. Dashboards therefore see either the whole night or none of it.
sonnet.q11: The retry reruns the whole nightly from the start. Extract empties `stg_orders` first, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. If merge failed, its transaction rolled back. The retry marks any stale `running` row for the same night `failed`. The retry extracts rows with `updated_at` later than the mark minus 2 hours, and the mark has not moved.
sonnet.q12: It empties `stg_orders`, then copies all orders of the differing creation days from the replica into it. It merges them as in step 2 (upsert by `order_id` where the staged `updated_at` is at least the existing one). It does not move the mark.
